name: Defias Hideout
summary: Defias thugs and vagrants linger in a ruined house on Moonbrook’s southern edge. Its upper floor hides a route into the chambers beneath the town.

sections.title: A Gateway in Ruin
sections.body: The Defias Hideout hides Edwin VanCleef’s southern operations beneath a ruined house in Moonbrook. Vagrants and Defias thugs move through its ransacked rooms, much like those of any other manor or farmhouse in the settlement. On the upper floor, an opening leads down into the winding passages of the Deadmines. The Brotherhood keeps most of its strength around Moonbrook’s perimeter and at work underground, so few guards remain inside. They watch the hideout as a narrow passage into the mines, not as a stronghold of its own.

faq.q: What is inside the Defias Hideout?
faq.answer: A staircase inside the house leads to a winding tunnel and the overland entrance to the Deadmines. Vagrants wander through the mostly bare building, with a few bandits nearby.

faq.q: Why is the hideout relatively unguarded inside?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood keeps its fighters in Moonbrook’s streets to intercept intruders, while its laborers and enforcers work deep in the mines.

faq.q: Where in Moonbrook is this building located?
faq.answer: The hideout stands on Moonbrook’s southern edge in southwestern Westfall, near the base of the mountains. It is a large, intact, two-story building.

faq.q: Who are the people lingering around the hideout?
faq.answer: Defias bandits and desperate vagrants linger in the building and around Moonbrook. Some vagrants fled poverty; others joined the Brotherhood out of necessity.

angles.text: As a rogue, you can see how the Defias hide the gateway to a vast underground fortress inside a plain ruined manor, keeping its scale from casual Stormwind patrols.
As an Alliance adventurer, you can trace Edwin VanCleef’s conspiracy to this crumbling estate, a key staging ground in the effort to end the Defias rebellion.
